# ctables/toolchain

> How to build: compile the C with `cc -O2`.

truck [ctables](../ctables.md) · [source](../../../registry/ctables/toolchain.pkg)

  The source is written to `prog.c` in a temporary directory, so builds
  are reproducible. The flags matter:

  - `-std=gnu11`: statement expressions `({ ... })` are a GNU extension,
    supported by GCC and Clang;
  - `-fwrapv`: integer overflow wraps, as Packenger defines it;
  - `-fno-strict-aliasing`: memory is read and written through casts;
  - `-w`: the generated code has unused labels and variables.

  The executable links with the C library, dynamically.

## Emit variants

The first variant whose condition holds is used.

### `emit file`

```nasm
prog.c
```

### `emit`

```nasm
cc -std=gnu11 -O2 -fwrapv -fno-strict-aliasing -w -o {out} prog.c
```
